result:
I built the adapter. On the real file, `Adapter(file_path="raw/atlanta_directory_2026-06-14.xls").run()` returns **864 Black-owned firms** from 2,888 data rows, and all 17 tests pass. `adapter.py`, `test_adapter.py` and `NOTES.md` are in the working directory.

- **The file isn't really Excel.** Despite the `.xls` name, it's an HTML table in Windows-1252 encoding, so the adapter parses it as HTML with the standard library.
- **Filter:** a firm counts as Black-owned if any of its rows has `Certification Type` = `AABE` (African American Business Enterprise). There is no separate ethnicity column. I excluded SBE (small business), FBE (female-owned), HABE (Hispanic), APABE (Asian/Pacific) and NABE (Native American).
- **Deduplication:** the file has one row per firm per certification, so most firms appear two or three times. The supplier ID can't be used to tell firms apart:
  - The placeholders `9999999` and `999999` are shared by 31 unrelated firms.
  - At least 9 other IDs are each shared by two unrelated firms.
  - Three firms appear under two different IDs each.

  I deduplicated on a cleaned-up company name instead. One extra rule merges a firm relisted under a longer name when the owner and email match exactly ("Anointed Professional Enterprise" became "…Enterprises Inc dba Glory…"). When a firm appears more than once, the record uses the AABE row with the latest expiration date.
- **Mapping:**
  - Owner name, city and state are built from the source columns.
  - `naics_code` is pulled from the commodity codes. A few codes have only 5 digits and look truncated; I passed them through unchanged.
  - Website entries that aren't web addresses (e.g. `http://no website`) are blanked, with the original text kept in `source_fields`.
  - Placeholder IDs become an empty `business_id`.

Decisions you may want to revisit:
- **Expired certifications are included.** 42 of the 864 firms had already expired before the 2026-06-14 download. Each record keeps the expiration date in `source_fields`, so they can be filtered out later.
- **`business_id` is not unique.** Four IDs each appear on two different Black-owned firms, and 18 firms have no ID because theirs was a placeholder.
- **Labels:** I set `CONFIDENCE` to `confirmed_black` because AABE is a city certification tied to ethnicity. I set `PROGRAM` to `MWBE`, the closest option the base class lists.
